newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mostly higher, soyoil falters.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mostly higher, soyoil falters.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended mostly higher on Monday, bolstered by gains in soybeans and ideas supplies remained tight, traders said.
Soyoil crumbled, weighed down by commercial selling and soymeal/soyoil spreading.
"The oil really has been and continues to run at an inverse to meal," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities in Iowa.
"The demand is for soymeal," he added. "We're crushing for meal and the oil has no place to go. The market feels comfortable with the amount of oil we have."
Soy products rallied sharply early and contract highs were notched in May and September meal at $297.70 a ton and $261.00, respectively, on ideas domestic and export demand were outpacing supplies.

But USDA's weekly soybean export inspections tally came in at 5.988 million bushels, well below trade expectations for 10 million to 14 million bushels. The figure knocked soybean futures lower and dragged soymeal and soyoil down as well.
Soymeal ended $3.40 a ton higher to $0.20 lower with July up $2.20 at $289.80. Soyoil closed 0.16 to 0.01 cent per lb lower with July off 0.15 at 25.16.
The new high for the May soymeal is $297.70, topping the previous high of $297.00 set on April 3 and the highest level for a nearby contract since 1988.

On the day, commercials were active buyers of soymeal. One trade source said the action was tied to cash sales. Cargill Inc bought 300 lots July, ADm and Continental Grain each bought 200 July and Central Soya bought 50 July, traders said.
Funds sold at least 2,000 lots soymeal with Merrill Lynch the featured seller of roughly 1,200 lots. Lee B. Stern sold 400 July and Refco Inc sold 100 July and 300 December.
In soyoil, commercials were largely on the sell side with ADM a seller of 350 lots July and 300 August. Cargill Inc sold 200 July and CIS sold 300 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 21,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 25,743 while soyoil volume was pegged at 21,000, against Friday's 19,150.
